主要内容: President Donald Trump has dealt a significant blow to the renewable energy industry by approving tariffs of up to 30% on solar equipment made abroad. This decision threatens to hinder a $28 billion industry that relies on foreign-sourced parts for 80% of its supply. The move marks one of the most impactful actions against renewables yet under Trump's administration. The tariffs are expected to raise costs for U.S. solar projects and potentially slow the growth of the sector. Bloomberg’s Lynn Doan reported on the decision, highlighting its potential impact on the industry. The approval of these duties comes as part of broader trade policies aimed at protecting domestic manufacturing. The renewable energy sector, particularly solar, has been a key focus of these policies, with the aim of reducing reliance on foreign imports. The tariffs could lead to increased costs for consumers and businesses that depend on solar technology. The decision has raised concerns among industry stakeholders, who argue that it may undermine the competitiveness of U.S. solar companies in the global market.
